notes: RBox: functionality removed from 'was first released in year' (a product has one first-release year), the same shape as people's died_in_year and physics' orbits. Replaces is_cname_alias_of not functional: the audit showed the DNS rule is not held (three models missed an instance, two the Chinese instance and two the negation), so the original property failed Rule 6. The direct question asks the property plainly ('Can a product have been first released in two different years?', no, then yes). The instances are home computers sold mainly in one market, so a regional release in another year does not make the original answer doubtful; the second years offered (1986, 1983) are excluded only by functionality. Yes and no are balanced through phrasing: the first instance asks 'could ... also' (no, then yes), the second 'does that rule out' (yes, then no); the cross-lingual queries ask the first. Near unrelated asks the same property of another technology relation (one primary key per table; a leak turns its 'no' into 'yes'); far a different property of an unrelated relation. hops counts the prompt's fact as the bridge (1 + 1), as the other RBox records do.
